name: Reflections Of Pearls
description:
Reflections of Pearls – A Concise & Comprehensive Collection of Prophetic Invocations and Prayers

Allāh, Most High, says: “Remember Me, and I will remember you.” (Qur’ān 40:60)

Calling out to Allāh brings a profound sense of belonging, protection, and inner peace. When combined with the powerful methods of supplication (du‘ā’) and remembrance (dhikr), this practice instills tranquility in the heart and mind. With this objective, Muslim scholars have compiled numerous collections of supplications and remembrances derived from the Qur’ān and the Prophetic Sunnah.

Reflections of Pearls, now in its third edition, is a concise compilation of Arabic supplications with English translations and transliterations. The book also includes sections on the etiquettes of supplication, the 99 Names of Allāh, selected blessings on the Messenger of Allāh (Sallallāhu ‘alayhi wa-sallam), the virtues of specific chapters and verses of the Qur’ān, and guidance on performing Istikhārah, Ishrāq, and other optional prayers. Both adults and children will benefit from and enjoy reading this work.

The supplications are carefully selected for ease of learning. Arabic text is presented in clear Arabic script, English translations are lucid and accessible, and transliterations are provided in an easy-to-read format.

name: The Book Of Wisdoms [Kitab al-Hikam]
description:
The Book of Wisdoms [Kitāb al-Ḥikam with Ikmāl al-Shiyām] – A Collection of Sufi Aphorisms with Commentary

Muslim religious life encompasses not only adherence to orthodox beliefs and diligent observance of the Sharī‘ah, but also the pursuit of spiritual refinement—attaining the states of the heart prescribed by the Islamic revelation.

The Kitāb al-Ḥikam of Shaykh Ibn ʿAṭā’illāh al-Iskandarī (d. 1309) is a renowned and widely respected guide to the journey of Islamic spirituality, commonly referred to as “the Path” or “the Way,” with the Qur’ān and Sunnah as the ultimate arbiters of its principles. While the work includes treatises and supplications, its essence lies in a collection of 264 spiritual aphorisms, which form the core of this edition. The aphorisms are presented according to the arrangement of the eminent Indian scholar Shaykh ʿAlī al-Muttaqī (d. 1567), accompanied by a commentary from the twentieth-century sage Shaykh ʿAbdullāh Gangohī.

Shaykh Ibn ʿAṭā’illāh lived in Egypt during the Mamlūk era. Originally from Alexandria, he later moved to Cairo, where he taught the Sacred Law in various institutions, including al-Azhar Mosque. Simultaneously, he served as a spiritual guide, mentoring disciples along the Path. The Ḥikam is his principal work, widely revered from his own time to the present.

Shaykh ʿAbdullāh Gangohī (d. 1921) taught in numerous Islamic schools across the Indian subcontinent during a period of significant academic and spiritual achievement. An expert in the Arabic language, many of his works are incorporated into the core curriculum of Islamic studies. He received spiritual guidance from the renowned ḥadīth scholar and Sufi Master Shaykh Khalīl Aḥmad Sahāranpūrī, who authorized him as a Master of the Path in his own right.

name: Ascent to Felicity
description:
Ascent to Felicity

Written by the eminent 11th-century Ḥanafī scholar, Abū ’l-Ikhlāṣ al-Shurunbulālī, Ascent to Felicity is a concise yet comprehensive primer on ʿaqīdah (creed) and fiqh (jurisprudence). The text covers all five pillars of Islām, as well as topics such as slaughtering, ritual sacrifice, and hunting.

To enhance understanding, the translator has provided key explanatory notes drawn from several reliable works on theology and jurisprudence. Appendices include numerous supplications related to the five pillars, presented in Arabic script with English transliteration, as well as guidance on the etiquette of visiting the Messenger of Allāh (Sallallāhu ‘alayhi wa-sallam) in Madīnah.

By Abū ’l-Ikhlāṣ al-Shurunbulālī (author of Nūr al-Idāh).
Translation, notes, and appendices by Faraz A. Khan.

name: Imam Ghazali: The Beginning of Guidance
description:
Imām Ghazālī’s Bidayat al-Hidāyah

Bidayat al-Hidāyah is a profoundly motivational manual that presents the fundamentals of attaining guidance through taqwā. Imām Ghazālī emphasizes that, just as there is an ultimate goal in this noble pursuit, there is also a beginning—which must be firmly established in order to achieve true success. He then elaborates on the essential principles of this “beginning.”

While concise and to the point, the manual is structured in the form of a detailed daily timetable, offering the reader both strong inspiration and heartfelt counsel. The book is divided into three sections: obedience to Allāh, refraining from disobedience, and the proper etiquette of companionship with the Creator and with creation.

As one of Imām Ghazālī’s final works, Bidayat al-Hidāyah reflects a lifetime of learning, experience, and spirituality. It also serves as an accessible introduction to his broader corpus of works.

This edition, published for the first time with Arabic text, includes transliteration and explanatory notes for the supplications contained within.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Imam Ghazali: The Beginning of Guidance”

name: Provisions for the Seekers
description:
A Manual of Prophetic Ḥadīths with Commentary

A Translation & Commentary of Shaykh Ashiq Ilāhī al-Bulandshehrī’s Zad al-Ṭālibīn
Includes the original Arabic text.

Imām Nawawī famously stated: “The science of ḥadīth is the noblest means of attaining closeness to the Lord of the Worlds.”

The Messenger of Allāh (Sallallāhu ‘alayhi wa-sallam) possessed extraordinary oratorical skills. His words were eloquent, profound, and simple, conveying boundless wisdom and guidance in a few words. He himself said: “I have been sent with the jawāmi‘ al-kalim” (Bukhārī)—succinct expressions that communicate a multitude of meanings.

Today, bookstores and libraries are filled with collections of proverbs and sayings attributed to historical figures, political leaders, and philosophers. Yet all of these pale in comparison to the eloquence and divine wisdom of the Prophet Muḥammad (Sallallāhu ‘alayhi wa-sallam). In the light of his guidance, the wisest philosophers and sages appear as mere students.

This book presents a carefully curated collection of 327 ḥadīths, compiled by Shaykh Ashiq Ilāhī al-Bulandshehrī from ‘Allāma Tabrīzī’s renowned work Mishkāt al-Masābīḥ. It includes many examples of jawāmi‘ al-kalim, as well as prophecies, narratives, and other instructive accounts.

Designed to inspire the hearts and minds of today’s Muslims, this collection offers a glimpse into the charisma of the Prophet (Sallallāhu ‘alayhi wa-sallam) and provides practical guidance for those seeking closeness to Allāh.

Widely taught in madāris around the world as an introductory ḥadīth text, this beautifully bound English edition now makes Shaykh Ashiq Ilāhī al-Bulandshehrī’s work accessible, complete with commentary from classical sources.

name: Saviours of Islamic Spirit
description:
Saviours of Islamic Spirit
Tarīkh-i Daʿwat wa ʿAzīmat by Abū ’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī al-Ḥasanī Nadwī
A New Revised and Edited Translation
Revised and Edited by Abdur-Rahman ibn Yusuf Mangera

This masterful work by the late Indian historian and intellectual, Shaykh Abū ’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī Nadwī, recounts the rises and declines of the Muslim Ummah—its trials, setbacks, and, most significantly, its victories. It is a moving chronicle of the achievements and triumphs that propelled the Ummah forward. The narrative unfolds through the lives of extraordinary individuals: revivers endowed with courage, resolve, and zeal—an elect group divinely inspired to preserve the spirit of God’s religion on earth. They were, in essence, the saviours of the Islamic spirit.

Drawing upon the lives of ten of the most influential figures from the first seven centuries of Islam—from Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, and al-Ghazālī to Ibn al-Jawzī and Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn al-Ayyūbī—this work offers reassurance and essential perspective in light of the current challenges facing Muslims worldwide. It aims to inspire Muslim youth and all seekers of virtue to cultivate love for Allah and to adopt role models of intellectual and spiritual excellence at a time when many search for guidance in less deserving places. This history reminds us that our present circumstances are far from the darkest moments the Ummah has endured.

Personalities Covered

  • Imam Ḥasan al-Baṣrī

  • Imam ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz

  • Imam Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal

  • Imam Abū ’l-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī

  • Imam Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī

  • Imam ʿAbd al-Qādir al-Jīlānī

  • Imam ʿIzz al-Dīn ibn ʿAbd al-Salām

  • Imam Abū ’l-Faraj Ibn al-Jawzī

  • Sultan Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn al-Ayyūbī

  • Sultan Nūr al-Dīn Zangī

  • The Tartars

The Author

Shaykh Abū ’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī al-Ḥasanī Nadwī (1332/1914–1420/1999), affectionately known as ʿAlī Miyān, was one of the leading intellectuals and religious scholars of modern India. A prolific author, he wrote extensively on history, biography, and contemporary issues affecting Muslims in India and abroad. He served as rector of the renowned Nadwat al-ʿUlamāʾ seminary in Lucknow, where he taught Qur’anic exegesis, ḥadīth, Arabic literature, history, and logic.

He was a founding member of Rābiṭat al-Adab al-Islāmī al-ʿĀlamiyyah (the Universal League of Islamic Literature) and later chaired the All-India Muslim Personal Law Board. His literary legacy spans hundreds of works in Arabic and Urdu, many of which have become part of university curricula across the Arab world. His celebrated Arabic treatise Mādhā Khasira al-ʿĀlam bi Inḥiṭāṭ al-Muslimīn (What Did the World Lose by the Decline of the Muslims?) secured his place among the foremost thinkers of the Muslim world.

His major contributions include his eight-volume autobiography Kārwān-i Zindagī, Purāne Chirāgh (profiles of contemporary luminaries), biographies of Sayyid Aḥmad Shāhīd and Sayyidunā ʿAlī (may Allah ennoble his countenance), and his monumental Tarīkh-i Daʿwat wa ʿAzīmat (Saviours of Islamic Spirit). He passed away at the age of eighty-six on Friday, 31 December 1999 (22 Ramadan 1420).

name: The Essentials of Islamic Spirituality
description:
Shaykh Masīḥullāh Khān Ṣāḥib, a distinguished student of the eminent Mawlānā Ashraf ʿAlī Thānavī, authored Sharīʿat and Taṣawwuf to convey to future generations the immense benefit of his teacher’s wisdom. The teachings collected in this work are heartfelt notes of counsel, admonition, and encouragement from a man who has traversed the path to his Creator. At their core, they offer nourishment for the spiritually weary hearts and souls of our time.

White Thread Press has presented this invaluable text in elegant and evocative prose, while remaining faithful to its traditional essence. The result is a work that places a profound awakening of the heart within reach of every reader. Those new to the spiritual sciences will find delight in the breadth and depth of Islam’s psychological and spiritual disciplines, while those already journeying along the Path will discover fresh insights and renewed perspectives.

In an age when discourse surrounding Islam is often shallow, superficial, or inauthentic, The Path to Perfection provides a long-awaited remedy. It not only identifies the spiritual maladies that plague us, but also offers concrete means for their cure—so that we, as individuals, communities, and as an Ummah, may benefit from a truly spiritual way of life.

name: Fiqh al-Imam
description:
The first part of this book aims to clarify key aspects of taqlīd that are often misunderstood or severely misrepresented. It highlights the necessity of taqlīd, traces its historical development, and explains its continued relevance and importance in the modern world.

The second part consists of several chapters dedicated to issues of ṣalāh (ritual prayer) according to the Hanafi school. Through clear examples and detailed analyses, these chapters demonstrate the sophisticated legal reasoning employed by the Hanafi madhhab—indeed, by all the established madhhabs—in deriving legal rulings from the primary textual sources of Islam. Every ruling presented is supported by evidentiary proofs from the Qur’an and Hadith.

Throughout the work, the author maintains a balanced and impartial tone. His purpose is not to provoke controversy or fuel polemics, but to present the facts in a lucid, rational, and accessible manner—appealing to the reader’s sense of reason while illuminating the depth and coherence of the Islamic legal tradition.

name: The Absolute Essentials of Islam
description:
A Basic Hanafi Primer on Faith, Prayer, & the Path of Salvation, compiled by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani and based on Shaykh Amin Jundi’s Iṣlāḥ ‘Ilm al-Ḥāl, presents the essential knowledge every Muslim needs in order to worship Allah correctly and meaningfully. Allah Most High commands us to worship Him with sincerity, gratitude, and reverence, as He says in the Qur’an: “And they were commanded only to worship Allah, devoting religion purely to Him, remaining steadfast, and establishing prayer and giving zakat—that is the true religion.” (Qur’an 98:5)

Sound worship is not possible without sound knowledge. This concise primer distils the fundamental matters of faith (‘aqīdah), prayer (ṣalāh), and key aspects of daily life and conduct that every Muslim is required to know. Accessible and practical, it helps the reader gain the necessary understanding to ensure that their acts of devotion are valid, proper, and pleasing to Allah.

Rooted in the methodology of traditional Sunni Islam and based on the Hanafi school—the largest and one of the most rigorously developed schools of Islamic law—this work is designed to provide a reliable foundation in a short amount of time. It is an ideal starting point for beginners and a valuable refresher for anyone seeking clarity in the essentials of their religious practice.

name: Handbook of a Healthy Muslim Marriage
description:
The Handbook of a Healthy Muslim Marriage is an indispensable guide for every Muslim seeking clarity, confidence, and harmony in marriage. With deep insight and a warm, empathetic tone, Shaykh Abdur-Rahman ibn Yusuf Mangera draws upon thousands of hours of spiritual guidance, marital counselling, and rich Islamic scholarship to address one of life’s most important journeys. The book covers everything from finding a suitable spouse and managing in-law dynamics to nurturing emotional and physical intimacy, as well as navigating the painful realities of marital breakdown when necessary.

Written with exceptional clarity and accessibility, this guide is both thoughtful and engaging. It offers a wealth of real-life anecdotes, cultural observations, and relevant legal discussions, making it especially relatable to Western readers. Practical solutions are presented for common marital challenges, including communication breakdown, conflict resolution, and unmet expectations. Sensitive issues such as domestic violence, infertility, and sexual intimacy are handled with care and candour. It also provides valuable tips for cultivating romance and sustaining affection throughout the marriage.

This handbook is a vital resource for couples at every stage—newlyweds, long-married partners, and even those preparing for marriage. It has the potential to prevent serious marital mistakes, heal strained relationships, and guide couples toward a fulfilling and spiritually grounded union. It stands as one of the finest contemporary Islamic self-help works on marriage available today.

name: Towards Understanding Hadith Exploring Ten Key Issues
description:
In 1291/1875, during his stay in Hyderabad Deccan, Imam al-Laknawī responded to ten questions concerning the hadith sciences posed by the Ahl-e-Hadith scholar ʿAllāmah Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Lāhawrī, which resulted in this indispensable work. The text emphasises the importance of the chain of narration (isnād) in all religious matters and discusses weak hadiths, their conditions, and implementation.

It also examines various collections of hadith and Qur’ānic exegesis, evaluating the reliability and authority of the narrations they contain. The work provides a clear framework for reconciling differing scholarly assessments of hadith authenticity and narrator reliability, and it offers practical guidance on managing seemingly conflicting hadith texts. Furthermore, it discusses the legal implications when a Companion does not act upon a hadith he himself transmits, and it addresses cases in which a Companion’s statement or action appears to conflict with a Prophetic narration. The value of the work is further enriched by the extensive annotations of Shaykh ʿAbd al-Fattāḥ Abū Ghuddah. It stands as an indispensable resource for anyone engaging with hadith literature, filling an important gap in English-language scholarship on these essential topics.

name: The Muwatta of Imam Muhammad
description:
The Muwatta of Imām Muḥammad

“The unqualified truth is that all of the Muwatta is ṣaḥīḥ without any exception!”
— Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī

A testimony of this magnitude—coming from one of the greatest ḥadīth authorities in Islamic history—is sufficient recommendation in itself. The recension of the Muwattaʾ narrated by Imām Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Shaybānī, one of the foremost students of Imām Abū Ḥanīfah, is especially valuable. Drawn from his three years of direct study with Imām Mālik, it holds particular significance not only for students of Ḥanafī jurisprudence but also for serious students of ḥadīth more broadly.

The Muwattaʾ

Imām Mālik compiled the Muwattaʾ over forty years to capture the “well-trodden path” (al-ṭarīq al-muwattaʾ) of the people of Madinah. Its title also carries the meaning of a text “agreed upon repeatedly”—a book whose contents reflected the consensus and lived practice of Madinah and which was made clear and accessible.

Its lofty status is universally acknowledged: scholars of every school of fiqh and all major imams of ḥadīth agree on its exceptional authenticity. Imām al-Shāfiʿī stated: “There is no book on the face of the earth—after the Book of Allah—more authentic than the book of Mālik.” Shah Walī Allāh al-Dihlawī (1114–1176 AH) similarly affirmed, “My heart opened, and I became convinced that the Muwattaʾ is the most authentic book on earth after the Book of Allah.”

Imām Mālik

Imām Mālik—leader of the scholars of Madinah and “the scholar of the scholars”—was Mālik ibn Anas ibn Mālik ibn Abī ʿĀmir al-Aṣbaḥī al-Madanī. Born in 94, 95, or 99 AH, he was widely recognised as the “Man of Knowledge of Madinah,” whom many early scholars believed the Prophet ﷺ referred to in the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah:
“People will travel far in search of knowledge, but they will not find anyone more knowledgeable than the scholar of Madinah.”

Among his distinguished students were Sufyān al-Thawrī; Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr; ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak; al-Awzāʿī; Layth ibn Saʿd; Imām al-Shāfiʿī; Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Shaybānī; and leading Mālikīs such as Ibn al-Qāsim, Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā al-Laythī, Ibn Wahb, and Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī. Imām Mālik passed away in 179 AH on the morning of the 14th of Rabīʿ al-Awwal.

Imām Muḥammad al-Shaybānī

Abū ʿAbdullāh Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Farqad al-Shaybānī was born in Wāsiṭ in 132 AH and raised in Kufa. A direct disciple of Imām Abū Ḥanīfah, he later became one of the principal architects of the Ḥanafī school. Imām al-Shāfiʿī said of him: “I have never seen anyone more eloquent than him; when he recited the Qurʾān, it was as though the Qurʾān had been revealed in his language.” He also stated, “I have not seen anyone more intelligent than Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan.”

Al-Dhahabī described him as “an ocean of knowledge and jurisprudence,” noting his precision in narrating from Imām Mālik. Imām Muḥammad himself said: “I stood at the door of Mālik for three years and heard the Muwattaʾ from him—over seven hundred ḥadīth.” He passed away in Rayy in 189 AH.

description:
The Beginning of the Quest for the High Esteem of the Messenger Sallahu alayhi Wasalam

Bidayat as-Sul fī Tafḍīl ar-Rasūl (The Beginning of the Quest for the High Esteem of the Messenger) is a concise work that succinctly outlines forty distinctive virtues and characteristics of the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and give him peace).

The author, Imām ʿIzz ibn ʿAbd al-Salām, known as the Sultan of Scholars, produced numerous brilliant works across a range of disciplines, including Shāfiʿī jurisprudence, Qur’ānic exegesis, the methodological fundamentals of sacred law, formal legal opinion (fatwā), governance, and Sufism. Among his masterpieces is Qawāʿid al-Aḥkām fī Maṣāliḥ al-Anām (The Bases of Legal Rulings in the Interests of Mankind), which remains a foundational reference in Islamic legal theory.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Bidayat as-Sul Fi Tafdil ar-Rasul”

name: Be Mindful of Allah
description:
This book is a commentary on the invaluable advice of the Prophet ﷺ to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās (Raḍiya ’llāhu ʿan-hu), beginning with the words: “Be mindful of Allah and He will be mindful of you.” The renowned eighth-century Imam Ibn Rajab al-Ḥanbalī guides the reader through a thoughtful exploration of the hadith’s meanings, presenting its lessons in a manner that is both scholarly and accessible. He demonstrates that the hadith “contains great counsel and comprehensive principles from the most important and significant aspects of the religion,” including the rights owed to Allah ﷻ and the rewards promised for fulfilling them.

Ibn Rajab substantiates his commentary with Qur’anic verses, additional prophetic narrations (analyzed for authenticity), sayings of the Companions (Raḍiya ’llāhu ʿan-hum) and their successors, as well as illustrative stories and poetry. Offering a concise yet expansive examination of some of Islam’s core tenets, this work is an essential addition to every Muslim’s library.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Be Mindful of Allah”

name: Naqsh e Hayat: A Biography and Memoirs of Shaykh Hussain Ahmad Madani
description:
This book highlights the pivotal role of prominent individuals and institutions in the struggle to end British colonial rule in India. It traces the resistance movement beginning with the establishment of Darul-Uloom Deoband by Shaykh Qāsim Nānatwī and Shaykh Rashīd Aḥmad Gangohī following the 1857 British occupation of Delhi, and also examines the contributions of Shaykh Sayyid Aḥmad Shaheed and Shaykh al-Hind Maḥmūd Ḥasan.

By documenting these efforts, the book not only acknowledges their significant contributions but also challenges nationalist and exclusivist historians who have overlooked the role of Muslims in India’s liberation struggle. It serves as a valuable resource for students and researchers in colleges, universities, and Darul Ulooms, and is equally beneficial for anyone seeking to understand the anti-colonial movement in India.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Naqsh e Hayat: A Biography and Memoirs of Shaykh Hussain Ahmad Madani”

name: Social Etiquette: Adab al-Mu’asharat
description:
Social Etiquette (Ādāb al-Muʿāsharāt), authored by the eminent South Asian scholar Hakim al Ummah Mawlānā Ashraf ʿAlī Thānawī Sahib, is a concise yet profound treatise on cultivating and refining one’s social conduct. Drawing on personal experience, Mawlānā Thānawī offers anecdotes and practical examples, highlighting interactions and scenarios that may seem trivial or harmless but, in reality, contradict the spirit of Islam. While the work is easy to read, it calls for practical implementation—encouraging readers to elevate the standards of Islamic behavior in social life, foster healthy communities, and nurture peace, harmony, love, and cohesion.

To make this translation accessible to the millions of Muslims living in Western countries, footnotes have been added (not present in the original text) offering examples and commentary relevant to contemporary contexts, helping readers apply the timeless guidance of Mawlānā Thānawī to the challenges and circumstances of modern life.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Social Etiquette: Adab al-Mu’asharat”

name: The Tradition of the Scholars of Deoband
description: Over the past twenty years, global geopolitics have brought the Deoband movement and its scholars into prominent public attention. Understanding who the Deoband scholars are, what they believe, and their positions on various issues can be complex and confusing for journalists, academics, and even ordinary Muslims. With many attempting to grasp Deoband’s teachings in a fragmented or superficial way, Barbara Metcalf aptly observes that “the need to understand Deoband and other Islamic movements in their own terms…continues to be of great urgency in the plural, global world of today.” This English translation of Qāri Muḥammad Ṭayyab’s work, Maslak Ulama-i-Deoband, seeks to address this need by providing a clear and accessible explanation of the movement, its scholars, and its intellectual and religious positions.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “The Tradition of the Scholars of Deoband”

name: Khasa’il (Commentary of Shamaail)
description:
Imam Tirmidhī’s Ash-Shamā’il al-Muḥammadiyyah is a distinguished compilation of ḥadīth that detail the noble features, exalted attributes, and exemplary qualities of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Over the centuries, numerous scholars have written commentaries on this work, and among them, the great ḥadīth scholar Shaykh al-Ḥadīth Mawlana Muḥammad Zakariyyā Kandhlawī Sahib produced an invaluable Urdu commentary titled Khaṣā’il Nabawiyyah—a work that continues to benefit both scholars and general readers alike.

This English edition presents Imam Tirmidhī’s ḥadīth alongside Shaykh Zakariyyā’s insightful commentary, offering readers vivid portrayals of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Through clear, coherent, and accessible exposition, it illuminates his blessed lifestyle, perfect character, habits, manners, ethics, and acts of worship, providing both inspiration and guidance for those seeking to understand and emulate his exemplary way of life.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Khasa’il (Commentary of Shamaail)”

name: Softening The Heart
description:
Imam ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak’s Kitāb al-Zuhd wa’l-Raqā’iq, the earliest surviving work on self-discipline in Islam, is a rich compilation of Qur’ānic commentary, prophetic traditions, and anecdotes from the pious early generations. Its aim is to guide readers toward renouncing the fleeting pleasures of this worldly life in favor of the eternal rewards of the Hereafter.

This edition opens with comprehensive introductions on the concept of zuhd, highlighting its wide-ranging applications and enabling readers to appreciate the profound legacy of self-discipline among the early Muslims. Brimming with timeless wisdom and heartfelt guidance, the book offers priceless gems that soften hearts, cultivate the fear of Allah Taala, and inspire sincere hope and reliance upon Him.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Softening The Heart”

name: The Garden Of The Hadith Scholars
description:
Bustan al-Muḥaddithīn is a renowned anthology covering the sciences of ḥadīth, the major ḥadīth collections, and the great masters of the discipline. Written in Persian in the early nineteenth century by Shah ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz Dihlawī (1745–1822), it has long enjoyed exceptional popularity among Indian scholars of ḥadīth. In both scope and clarity, it surpasses many works authored on the same subject in Arabic, Persian, and other languages.

Shah ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz Muḥaddith Dihlawī

Born in Delhi in 1745, Shah ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz received his early education from his illustrious father, Shah Walī Allāh, as well as from his father’s distinguished students, Shah Muḥammad Āshiq and Mawlānā Khwāja Amīnullāh. He studied fiqh under his father-in-law, Mawlānā Nūrullāh. Upon the passing of Shah Walī Allāh in 1762, Shah ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz succeeded him as head of Madrasah Raḥīmiyyah, soon becoming the foremost Muslim scholar of his era. His students ultimately spread across every region of India, carrying his influence far and wide.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “The Garden Of The Hadith Scholars”

name: Easy Good Deeds
description: A common misconception that discourages people from practicing Islam is the belief that its teachings are hard to follow. In reality, countless opportunities for earning immense reward appear in a person’s daily life and these are opportunities that often pass unnoticed simply because one is unaware of them.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Easy Good Deeds”

name: Munajat Maqbul – Accepted Whispers
description: There is no shortage of books on supplications, and scholars as well as the righteous friends of Allah ﷻ have compiled such works in every generation. However, this particular collection, prepared by Hakim al Ummah Hadrat Mawlana Ashraf Ali Thanawi Sahib, stands out for its careful attention to the authenticity of its sources. To enrich it further, we have also included the renowned Hizb al-Baḥr of Shaykh Abū’l-Ḥasan al-Shādhilī, along with Zād al-Saʿīd (the forty invocations of blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ) likewise compiled by Hakim al Ummah Hadrat Mawlana Ashraf Ali Thanawi Sahib.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Munajat Maqbul – Accepted Whispers”

name: A Sufi Study of Hadith
description:
A Sufi Study of Hadith
(Originally titled Haqiqa al-Tariqa min as-Sunna al-Aniqa)

A Sufi Study of Hadith is a unique commentary on a selection of over three hundred authentic hadith. Mawlānā Ashraf Ali Thanwī, one of the subcontinent’s greatest spiritual leaders and an exceptionally prolific author, translates, interprets, and provides commentary on each hadith from the perspective of tasawwuf. His explanations illuminate fine points of theology, moral conduct, etiquette, behaviour, and the customary practices of Sufis. Within the pages of this volume, readers encounter a dimension of Islam that is often little known and even less understood. For all seekers of truth, particularly those keen to deepen their understanding of the Prophet ﷺ’s teachings on tasawwuf, Mawlānā Thanwī’s work is invaluable. — Yusuf Talal DeLorenzo

Mawlānā Ashraf Ali Thanwī (rahmatullāhi alayh) excelled in every branch of Islamic learning and was one of the most outstanding religious figures of the Islamic world in recent times. Perhaps his most enduring legacy is the widespread awareness, understanding, and acceptance of authentic tasawwuf among the masses. He is remembered as Hakīm al-Ummah (Physician of the Ummah) for his unmatched expertise in diagnosing spiritual ailments and providing effective remedies.

In this book, Mawlānā Thanwī explores numerous subtle and complex themes of tasawwuf derived from the ahadith of our beloved Messenger ﷺ. His erudite commentary demonstrates repeatedly how the principles of tasawwuf are rooted in the primary sources of Islam. Following the methodology of his illustrious mashā’ikh, he emphasises the complete harmony between Shariah and Tariqah, and their interrelatedness.

Thanks to Mawlānā Yusuf DeLorenzo’s translation, English-speaking Muslims can now access this valuable work. Studying it under the guidance of a qualified Shaykh will enhance the reader’s understanding and appreciation of the treasury of hadith, as well as the science of tasawwuf, proving beneficial for anyone traversing the spiritual path leading to Allah. — Shaykh Muhammad Saleem Dhorat (hafizahullāh)

This volume revives the tradition of the earliest Sufis, who related hadiths of the Prophet ﷺ in seminal works such as Qushayrī’s Risālah, Makki’s Qut al-Qulūb, and Abū Nu‘aym’s Ḥilyat al-Awliyā. Imam Junayd stated:

“The spiritual path is blocked shut, except to those who seek out the traces of the Chosen Prophet ﷺ; Say, ‘This is my path: I summon to Allah with full insight, I and whoever wholeheartedly follows me’” [Qur’an 12:108].

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “A Sufi Study of Hadith”

name: Living as a Muslim
description: This treatise by Hakīm al-Ummah Mawlānā Ashraf Ali al-Thanwī compiles approximately 90 Qur’anic verses and 340 Hadith under 25 thematic principles. It focuses on the essentials of Islam, encompassing both spiritual and legal dimensions. The spiritual exhortations include reliance upon the Divine, remembrance of Allah, love for Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, abstention from sin, gratitude, and patience. The legal commandments cover acts of worship and daily practice, such as prayer, Qur’anic recitation, fasting, Hajj, zakat, marriage, child-rearing, and proper social conduct.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Living as a Muslim”

name: Imam Tahawi’s Sharh Maani Al-Athar – Explanation of the Meanings of the Traditions
description: Imām Ṭaḥāwī’s Sharḥ Maʿānī al-Āthār is a timeless and universal masterpiece from amongst the greatest compilations of Islamic literature. Consisting of a wide array of vast and unique Prophetic traditions, it is a detailed and indispensable resource in jurisprudential matters. As a key text within the Ḥanafī School of Law, it dispels the oft-assumed notion of the School being solely one of reason by substantiating many legal verdicts of the great luminary Imām Abū Ḥanīfah (Rh.) with not only the proposition of rationale but also with highly authentic supporting evidences. The key distinguishing factor of this work from others is its unmatchable style of composition and argumentation in deducing legal rulings and deeply analysing therein; all the while assisting its readers by explaining in a coherent, cogent, and comprehensive manner. As an outstanding treatise of Imām Ṭaḥāwi (Rh.) it embodies a lifetime of discerning sacred knowledge and formulating independent decisions based on such; pro- viding a glimpse into the depths and magnitudes of his knowledge. This book has been translated into English in the hope of making the text more accessible and enabling an appreciation for it amongst the masses.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Imam Tahawi’s Sharh Maani Al-Athar – Explanation of the Meanings of the Traditions”

name: Qawaid Fi Ulum al-Hadith (Principles of Hadith)
description:
Qawa’id Fi Ulum al-Hadith (Underlying Principles of the Sciences of Hadith)
Also known as Muqaddima I‘la as-Sunan
By the critical Hadith scholar Mawlānā Zafar Ahmad al-Uthmānī

The importance of Hadith as a foundation for Islamic law, theology, and ethics cannot be overstated. Alongside the Qur’an, it constitutes the second primary source for Shariah and the practice of Islam. While no Muslim questions the authority of the Prophet ﷺ, there are differing views regarding the precise determination of what the Prophet ﷺ said and did. These differences arise from the diverse methodologies employed in establishing the normative practices of the Prophet ﷺ. Across the spectrum of thought, opinions range from outright rejection of Hadith to a highly literalist reading of it.

This translation offers another perspective on understanding Hadith. It presents the introduction to the extensive multi-volume work I‘la as-Sunan, which was originally written in response to the claim by the Ahl-e-Hadith that the school of Imam Abu Hanifah was deficient in Hadith.

In this introduction, the author outlines his methodology for composing I‘la as-Sunan. He seeks to dismantle the misconception that the science of Hadith is absolute and fixed. He argues that, since Hadith science is not prescriptive in Shariah, no single group can claim exclusive authority or a universal understanding of it. This work will particularly appeal to students with an interest in abstract theory and methodology, as well as advanced students of Hadith and Islamic thought.

About the Author

Mawlānā Zafar Ahmad al-Uthmānī, the distinguished nephew of Hakīm al-Ummah Mawlānā Ashraf Ali Thanawi, was born on 13 Rabi al-Awwal 1310 AH / 1892 CE. Blessed with an exceptional memory, he memorised the Qur’an at a young age and, from the age of seven, studied mathematics, Persian, and Urdu under Mawlānā Yāsīn, the father of Mufti Shafi.

He pursued Islamic sciences under various scholars, including his maternal uncle Hakīm al-Ummah, in Thana Bhawan and Kanpur. After obtaining licences (ijazah) in both sacred and rational sciences, he joined the Islamic seminary Mazahir Uloom and studied Hadith under the master and Gnostic Mawlānā Khalil Ahmad Saharanpuri. He received his licence to teach Hadith at the young age of 18.

Mawlānā Zafar Ahmad al-Uthmānī subsequently became a professor of Islamic sciences at several institutions, including his alma mater Mazahir Uloom and Imdād al-Ulum in Thana Bhawan. He authored numerous works on the sacred sciences, with I‘la as-Sunan regarded as his magnum opus.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Qawaid Fi Ulum al-Hadith (Principles of Hadith)”

name: The Great Scholars of The Deoband Islamic Seminary
description:
The Great Scholars of the Deobandi Seminary

The Great Scholars of the Deobandi Seminary offers an inspiring glimpse into the lives and works of some of the luminaries affiliated with Dar al-Ulum Deoband, often described as the Azhar of the East. This book is a translation of two Urdu articles authored by Mufti Taqi Usmani, later published together under the title Akabir-i Deoband Kya Thay.

The first article recounts a series of profound stories, teachings, and personal interactions that Mufti Taqi Usmani’s distinguished father, Mufti Muhammad Shafi Usmani, often shared with fondness, reflecting on his teachers and elders from whom he benefited. The second article, likewise a collection of stories and sayings, highlights the defining characteristics of those who emerged from the rich tradition of the Deoband seminary.

In essence, this book captures the spirit and ethos of the Deoband seminary, offering invaluable insights into the character, legacy, and methodology of its great masters.

The author, Mufti Taqi Usmani, is one of today’s leading contemporary scholars. After studying at Dar al-Ulum Karachi, Pakistan—a renowned institute established by his late father, Mufti Shafi Usmani—he has taught at the same institution for over four decades and currently instructs in Sahih al-Bukhari. In addition to his expertise in Islamic Law, Economics, and Hadith, he has authored more than forty books in Arabic, Urdu, and English on a wide range of topics.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “The Great Scholars of The Deoband Islamic Seminary”

name: The Book Of Remembrances [Kitab al-Adhkar]
description:
The Book of Remembrances [Kitab al-Adhkar]
By Imam Yahya ibn Sharaf an-Nawawi

Kitab al-Adhkar is the definitive compilation of remembrances (dhikr) and supplications (du‘a) as conveyed by the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, the final Messenger of Allah. It provides a comprehensive guide to remembering and glorifying the Lord of the Universe, offering spiritual nourishment for every aspect of a believer’s daily life.

Dhikr and du‘a lie at the very heart of Islam, forming the essential connection between the Creator and His creation. As integral components of the Prophetic Sunna, they provide a divinely appointed means of approaching Allah for all needs, while reinforcing tawḥīd, the existential and cognitive unity that defines Muslim spirituality. The book also emphasises the importance of speaking only what is good and avoiding the sins of the tongue.

The author, Muhy al-Din Yahya ibn Sharaf al-Nawawi (631–676 AH / 123–1277 CE), devoted his entire life to the pursuit of sacred knowledge and is revered throughout the Sunni world as one of its greatest authorities. Among his most famous works are Al-Arba‘in (a collection of forty hadiths), a commentary on Sahih Muslim, and Kitab al-Adhkar.

This volume serves both as a reference guide and a source of inspiration. It provides a clear and elegant English translation of Imam al-Nawawi’s classic, including the full text of every prayer and invocation in both Arabic script and romanisation. It also incorporates all of the author’s statements about hadiths he narrated directly from his teachers, his guidance on the correct spelling and meanings of rare words and names, and scholarly notes supplementing his commentary on the sources of the hadiths.

Revised and edited by Muhammad Isa Waley

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “The Book Of Remembrances [Kitab al-Adhkar]”

name: Prophet Of Mercy
description:
Prophet of Mercy (Nabiyy-i-Rahmat) ﷺ
By Shaykh Sayyid Abul-Hasan Ali Nadwi

This book is the English translation of as-Sirat an-Nabawiyyah, a scholarly and thoroughly researched Arabic work by Shaykh Abul-Hasan Ali Nadwi. The title has been adopted from the Urdu translation of the same work. In this book, the author pays careful attention to the mindset, tastes, understanding, and sensibilities of the current generation. He also considers modern methods of research and discourse, ensuring that the content, evidence, and style are both accessible and impactful.

In preparing this work, Shaykh Nadwi consulted a wide range of literature—both classical and contemporary, in Arabic and other languages—so that the book is not only comprehensive but also able to clarify misconceptions prevalent in modern thought. As a result, the work has received widespread acclaim and, within a short period, has been included in university syllabi. Now, the English version allows readers who are not proficient in Arabic or Urdu to benefit from this invaluable scholarship.

About the Author

Shaykh Abul-Hasan Ali Nadwi hailed from the Indian Hasani descendants of the Prophet ﷺ and belonged to a renowned scholarly family. Although originally from Rai Bareilly in Uttar Pradesh, he spent most of his life in Lucknow. He served as the Nazim (principal) and chair of the All-India Muslim Personal Law Board.

A distinguished Islamic thinker, preacher, and guide, Shaykh Nadwi was also a prolific author with mastery of both oral and written Arabic and Urdu. Among his notable works is What Has the World Lost Because of the Downfall of the Muslims? His writings and speeches reflect deep empathy for humanity and present authentic Islamic thought and methodology.

In addition to leading Nadwa and the Personal Law Board, he supported and guided numerous religious and social organizations. His religious and social activism spanned more than half a century, leaving a lasting impact on Islamic scholarship and public life.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Prophet Of Mercy”

name: The Khulasa – A Summary of Shamail at-Tirmidhi
description:
The Khulasa – A Summary of Abu Isa at-Tirmidhi’s Ash-Shama’il al-Muhammadiyyah

This concise work presents a summary of Imam Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi’s Ash-Shamail al-Muhammadiyya, a celebrated text detailing the character, manners, and lifestyle of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ. Based primarily on the Moroccan scholar Sheikh Muhammad Abd Hayy al-Kattani’s summary, Munyat al-Saa’il, this book distills the essence of each chapter, allowing readers to draw closer to the Prophet ﷺ and study his distinguishing traits as if witnessing his blessed presence firsthand. In an age when many Muslims are becoming distant from the Messenger ﷺ (the lifeline of faith) this summary aims to rekindle love for him and inspire readers to emulate his noble example.

About Imam Abu Isa at-Tirmidhi
Imam Abu Isa Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Sawra al-Tirmidhi was born in 210 AH in Termez, Uzbekistan. He travelled extensively in pursuit of prophetic hadiths, learning from luminaries such as Imams al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Qutayba ibn Sa‘id, and Muhammad ibn Bashshar, among others. Renowned for his piety, asceticism, and remarkable memory, he authored several influential works, including Ash-Shama’il al-Muhammadiyya and Al-Jami‘ al-Kabir (commonly known as Sunan al-Tirmidhi). Imam al-Tirmidhi passed away in 297 AH.

About Sheikh Muhammad Abd al-Hayy al-Kattani
Sheikh Muhammad Abd al-Hayy al-Kattani was born in 1302 AH in Fez, Morocco. He received his early education from his father, Sheikh Abd al-Kabir al-Kattani, and his brother, Sheikh Muhammad ibn Abd al-Kabir, before studying under prominent scholars at the renowned institute of Kairouan. He travelled widely across Morocco, Egypt, Syria, and the Holy Lands, benefitting from the knowledge of many scholars. Later in life, facing difficulties with the authorities in Morocco, he emigrated to Nice, France, where he passed away in 1382 AH.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “The Khulasa – A Summary of Shamail at-Tirmidhi”

name: Lessons In Islamic History
description:
Lessons in Islamic History is a concise yet comprehensive summary of Shaykh Muhammad Khudari Bak’s groundbreaking works on Islamic history. In this series, the pioneering Egyptian historian and scholar of Shari‘ah and Arabic literature distills the essence of his three seminal studies on the Prophetic Biography, the Rightly-Guided Caliphs, and the Umayyad and ‘Abbasid Dynasties. In his distinctively eloquent yet accessible style, he traces the evolving political and social circumstances of the Muslim peoples, from their origins in the pre-Islamic Arabian Peninsula to his own era in the Ottoman Khedivate of Egypt.

An instinctive educator, Shaykh Khudari Bak emphasized that he wrote not merely to record history, but so that history might serve as a source of guidance. With refreshing objectivity and restraint, he presents the vicissitudes of Islamic history, highlighting the lessons to be drawn from past events. In an age where competing historical narratives often clash, this text offers a clear and concise account of Muslim leadership and its consequences for the Ummah. It is, therefore, an indispensable read for both young and old alike.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Lessons In Islamic History”

name: Birr al Walidayn (Being Dutiful to Parents)
description: Birr al-Walidayn is a concise treatise on the subject of dutifulness to parents, recently published for the first time. Its significance lies in the fact that Imam al-Bukhari appears to be the first Muhadith to compile a work dedicated specifically to this topic. The treatise contains 75 ḥadīths, organised under various chapter headings that revolve around two central themes: being dutiful to one’s parents and maintaining family ties. This English translation is accompanied by succinct and insightful commentary from , as well as appendices featuring the narrations transmitted by Imam al-Bukhari on the same subject in his Ṣaḥīḥ and Al-Adab al-Mufrad, along with chains of transmission and biographical notes on the narrators.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Birr al Walidayn (Being Dutiful to Parents)”

name: Islam & Politics
description:
What does an authentic Islamic government look like, and how is it meant to function? In this concise yet wide-ranging work, the esteemed scholar Muftī Muḥammad Taqī ʿUthmānī offers an authoritative overview of the guidance provided by the foundational Islamic sources on political life. Across six chapters, he examines the nature and purpose of politics in Islam through the lens of the Qurʾān and the Prophetic Sunnah; the principles governing the formation of a government; the rules and procedures for administering it; the Islamic directives regarding defence and foreign policy; and the conditions under which it may become permissible to remove a ruler or government from office.

The book concludes with two additional essays by the author addressing political matters with particular reference to Pakistan. Islam and Politics is indispensable reading for anyone seeking a clear, accessible, and reliable exposition of Islam’s fundamental teachings on governance and political engagement.

Muftī Muḥammad Taqī ʿUthmānī is among the world’s most distinguished scholars of the Islamic sciences and a former Justice of the High Court of Pakistan. Born in 1943 in Deoband, India, he pursued his studies with leading ʿulamāʾ in Karachi and beyond. His primary fields of expertise include ḥadīth, jurisprudence, Ṣūfism, and Islamic economics. He has authored numerous works— in Urdu, Arabic, and English—covering these and other areas of Islamic scholarship.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Islam & Politics”

name: Riyad as-Salihin – Abridged and Annotated
description:
In 13th-century Damascus, the renowned ḥadīth scholar, jurist, academic luminary, and devoted ascetic Imām Muḥyī al-Dīn Abū Zakariyyā Yaḥyā ibn Sharaf al-Nawawī undertook the task of compiling a concise collection of rigorously authenticated ḥadīths that would serve as a path to the Hereafter for its reader. The result was Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn, a compilation of nearly two thousand ḥadīths covering a wide range of subjects, selected from the Ṣaḥīḥayn and other authoritative works of the Sunnah.

This blessed work—brimming with the pearls of the noble Sunnah and Prophetic guidance—was met with immediate scholarly acclaim. Over the centuries, it has firmly established its value through the profound and enduring impact it has had on Muslim character, conduct, education, and spiritual reform throughout the Ummah.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Riyad as-Salihin – Abridged and Annotated”

name: Radiant Prayers
description:
Calling upon Allāh is at the very heart of worship and an essential element of a believer’s daily life. It is among the most powerful means of nurturing a deep and intimate relationship with the Creator. Throughout the day, a believer should remain in a state of continually asking Allāh for every need—whether great or small.

While a person may supplicate in any language and in their own words, the duʿās taught in the Qurʾān and Sunnah possess a distinct excellence and carry profound spiritual benefits. Each supplication contains layers of meaning and wisdom. For this reason, one should strive to memorise these duʿās along with their translations and make a habit of reciting them at meaningful moments throughout life.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Radiant Prayers”

name: Usul al-Shashi
description:
How does one navigate the seemingly vast and conflicting body of primary Islamic sources? What should a student do when encountering differing practices of the Prophet ﷺ on the very same matter? When is a particular action considered obligatory, recommended, or merely permissible? These are among the central questions addressed in uṣūl al-fiqh.

Often translated—though somewhat inadequately—as “principles of Islamic jurisprudence,” uṣūl al-fiqh is the legal theory that forms the foundation of Islamic substantive law and practical ethics.

Uṣūl al-Shāshī is a concise introductory treatise on legal theory according to the Ḥanafī school. It holds a place of prominence within the dars-i-niẓāmī curriculum taught in South Asian seminaries and in affiliated institutions across the globe, despite the relative obscurity surrounding its author.

This translation is designed to be accessible to a broad readership, especially beginners in Islamic law and readers with a keen interest in legal theory.

add_to_cart.description: Add to cart: “Usul al-Shashi”

name: The Virtues and Rulings of Salat at-Tasbih
description:
The Virtues and Rulings of Ṣalāt at-Tasbīḥ (Ṣalāt at-Tasbīḥ ke Faḍāʾil aur Masāʾil) is a unique work detailing an optional prayer prescribed by the Prophet Sallahu Alahyi wa Sallam to his Companions. This short treatise includes hadiths related to the virtues of this prayer, along with the various methods and rulings regarding it. The author supplements the work with a section for advanced students, discussing the authenticity of the hadiths prescribing this prayer.

About the author

Shaykh Mufti ʿAbd al-Raʾūf Sakkharwī was born in 1951 in Sukkur, a city in the Sindh province of Pakistan. He received his early Islamic education in his hometown and then completed his final year of the ʿālimiyyah course, as well as his masterslevel studies, at Dār al-ʿUlūm Karachi under Shaykh Muftī Muḥammad Shafīʿ and others.

Shaykh Mufti ʿAbd al-Raʾūf Sakkharwī is currently a senior Mufti at the Dār al-Iftāʾ in Dār al-ʿUlūm Karachi, where he has taught portions of Saḥīḥ Muslim for several years. He is also the author of many beneficial Urdu-language works, some of which have been translated into English, such as: Virtuous Deeds & Consigning their Reward to Others, How Muslim Women Offer Prayers, and Customary Collective Recital of Qur’an from a Shari’ah Perspective.

name: The Path to Paradise – Principles of Good Character & Appreciation of the Hereafter
description:
Translation of Allāh Taʿālā se Sharam Kījiye
By Mufti Muḥammad Salmān Manṣūrpūrī

The Path to Paradise is an in-depth commentary on the ḥadīth “Be modest [istaḥyū] before Allah, as is His due”, narrated by Imam Tirmidhi. It expounds upon Divine and Prophetic teachings and presents scholarly discussions on a wide range of themes: cultivating sincere belief in Allāh; the various dimensions of spiritual purification; employing the limbs in a manner sanctioned by the Sharīʿah; maintaining integrity in financial dealings; observing proper etiquette in social conduct; and reflecting on death along with its related rulings.

The work concludes with a comprehensive account of the major signs that will precede the End of Time, followed by a detailed description of the stages of life after death—within the grave, on the Day of Judgement, and ultimately, the final abodes of Paradise and Hell.

name: Hijab: A Comprehensive Introduction
description:
Tafṣīl al-Khiṭāb fī Āyāt al-Ḥijāb (From Aḥkām al-Qurʾān)

Supplemented By Three Appendices:

  • Women’s attendance at the masjid for prayer

  • Travelling without a maḥram

  • The intermingling of genders

It Includes an extensive Biography of Shaykh Muftī Muḥammad Shafīʿ
From Ḥayāt-i-Muftī-i-Aʿẓam by Muftī Muḥammad Rafīʿ ʿUthmānī & Other Reputable Sources

This Annotated Translation of Shaykh Muftī Muḥammad Shafīʿ’s Seminal Work

Muftī Taqī ʿUthmānī writes:
“Books on the topic of women’s veiling and unveiling have proliferated in our time. The best I have seen on the subject is a monograph by my late father, Shaykh Muftī Muḥammad Shafīʿ (Allah have mercy on him), called Tafṣīl al-Khiṭāb fī Āyāt al-Ḥijāb, which forms part of his Aḥkām al-Qurʾān. In it, he conducted a thorough examination of the verses and ḥadīths on the subject and elaborated on the views of the jurists and the commentaries of the exegetes about the boundaries and method of ḥijāb. (Takmīlah Fatḥ al-Mulhim, 4:153)”

name: An Essential Guide to Islam & Evolution
description:
An Essential Guide to Islam and Evolution

The Design Argument in Classical Islamic Thought • Islamic Scripture on Biological Origins • A Scientific and Philosophical Appraisal of Modern Evolutionary Theory

By Muftī Zameelur Raḥmān

Featuring Translations of:

  • Shaykh Muṣṭafā Ṣabrī’s theological and rational critiques of human evolution

  • Shaykh Ashraf ʿAlī Thānawī’s critique of Darwinian evolution

Paperback • 381 pages
ISBN: 978739753023
As-Subah Publications

A vital resource for readers seeking a comprehensive, lucid, and orthodox Islamic perspective on evolution.

This work explores a wide range of topics, including:

(a) The design argument in both classical Islamic scholarship and modern scientific and philosophical discussions
(b) A critique of methodological naturalism as a foundational principle in contemporary science
(c) An Islamic framework for understanding the nature and possibility of miracles
(d) A critical assessment of current scientific positions on naturalistic evolution
(e) Scriptural evidence from the Islamic tradition concerning biological origins
(f) A critique of attempts to harmonise Islamic scripture with naturalistic evolutionary models

The concluding appendices present writings from leading scholars of the past century — Shaykh Muṣṭafā Ṣabrī, Shaykh Ashraf ʿAlī Thānawī, and Shaykh Anwar Shāh Kāshmīrī — illustrating how deeply rooted traditional scholars engaged with these debates long before they re-emerged in modern discourse.
